fullText:
Get "Mathematics of Machine Learning" here: https://t.co/07exFk5LqL by @TivadarDanka v/ @PacktDataML
—
GitHub: https://t.co/2ENjzhr35C
—
Here is my review:

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗲𝘁 𝗢𝗳 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗔𝗹𝗴𝗼𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗺𝘀 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻 𝗙𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲

This massive book is incredible, with its comprehensive coverage of numerous fields of mathematics and their intersection with the world of AI, data science, and machine learning (AI+DSML). I remember the very first time that I encountered machine learning. This was 20+ years ago, and that was already after 20+ years of being drenched in advanced mathematics as an astrophysicist. 

That first encounter of mine with ML was this definition: "Machine learning is the set of mathematical algorithms that learn from experience" (slightly paraphrased from the original quote by Tom Mitchell, CMU). That definition surprised me, confused me, motivated me, and changed the course of my career from astrophysics into AI+DSML. 

This book by Tivadar Danka captures the full meaning of that definition. The book covers thoroughly the many areas and domains of mathematics through which patterns in data are detected, described, learned, and recognized - all for the benefit of powering ML and AI algorithms, applications, and aspirations. 

This book will motivate you, surprise you, and inspire you in many ways, no matter what level of mathematics has (or has not) already propelled your career journey. There is room for all of us to grow. 

This is a great book, worthy to sit on everyone's desktop, ready to help you explore and exploit the full set of mathematical algorithms that learn from experience. 

The book is accompanied by a rich GitHub code repository of Jupyter notebooks. Learn by doing! Do by learning!

Disclosure: the publisher provided me with a free review copy of the book.

Anthropic 发布了他们是如何反蒸馏的文章。

但是这文章也告诉我们，如何在一定程度上避免被封！

我们很多被封的用户，很大程度上是被系统误认为在对模型进行蒸馏而误封的，尤其是那些刚注册完就被快速封禁的账号。

你可以看一下如何避免某些操作，别让他们误以为你在做蒸馏，从而减少被封禁的风险：

不要让 Claude 展示思考过程，不要诱导它输出思维链

不要搬运或尝试篡改它的思维链，更不要反复尝试让它吐出思维过程

账号与付款方面：他们重点打击的是代理 IP 请求以及转售账号，所以账号注册和付款渠道要干净

环境隔离：不要在同一个 Agent 环境里同时共用国产模型和 Claude 模型

所以目前来看，最大的两个风险还是账号本身（包括付款渠道），以及在提示词中诱导模型展示思维链的操作

fullText:
很多人问我，随着玩 Grok bot 越来越多，什么时候订阅合适？

我一直都让大家再等等，但感觉现在时间到了。

他们终于推出了将 Twitter、Cursor、Grok bot 和 Grok 四合一的订阅，总共有 4 个档位：

$8（Plus）：包含 Twitter Premium
$30 (Premium)：Plus 的 4 倍用量
$100（Super）：Plus 的 15 倍用量
$200（Ultra）：Plus 的 50 倍用量

跟之前旧订阅的核心区别是，xAI 的 API 积分和 Cursor 的 API 积分会合并。

Cursor 依然有一些第三方模型，但相较于原始计划，第三方模型的用量大概率会缩减。

不过这次 Grok bot 的用量增加了：在 $30 以上的计划中，至少能获得双倍的 Grok bot 用量。

相较于你单独想用 Grok bot，如果你对 Cursor 及其第三方模型没有需求，只想要用 Grok bot 的话，我觉得是比较划算的，而且统一之后各种计算逻辑也能少点。

如果是之前通过 bug 订阅了 $99 会员的，就不要换；

没赶上之前旧方案的新增用户、想玩 Grok bot 的，我觉得可以换，毕竟确实比原来额度多了不少，而且更方便管理。

fullText:
"what would be done during the slowdown" is a good question, because i think people imagine beaurucrat-regulators sitting around on useless subcommittees and wasting the whole thing on wordcel slop analysis. in fact if you asked me two years ago, i would have suggested that is exactly what would happen. 

but these are scary times, and they call for us to think lofty & even impractical thoughts, that a 'sensible' person might have dismissed a few quarters ago. crises change the world overnight: the HFI has shifted something about the culture, broadly

this is something obvious that i missed, which is that the ai labs and the markets more generally just have just unbelievable pressure riding on the solving of alignment & control. even now, marginal improvements in alignment, safety, and model behavior are worth tremendous value to the labs. being able to convince themselves that the next training run is safe is the priority zero, one, and two in terms of capabilities progress right now. it's possible that will change and political will dissipates if some sense of comfort re-emerges after a period of relative safety (which would be a bad development; paranoia must be maintained through any potential periods of ai development where the models are too smart to reveal their behavioral predilections under scrutiny)

if there was a slowdown, it would ideally be channeled into some sort of tradeoff in which you can narrowly improve capabilities that prioritize risk-adjusted-return of alignment skills, mechinterp, monitorability, decision theory, behavioral generalization, etc. progress on all these areas is highly possible; automated alignment research is possible. the structure of the businesses may have to change, but all the trillion dollar ai behemoths of the world would shift their focus to doing this and only this at the behest of trillions of dollars in capital markets

fullText:
5 STEPS TO GET STARTED IN AGENTIC COMMERCE 

I almost never hit the panic button, but I am now. 

Agentic-first commerce is a game changer.

(Full episode on this is on Apple Podcasts, link below.)

What to do?

1. BUILD A COUNCIL OF LLMS ON YOUR OWN SERVERS.

If it’s not your model, it’s not your business. 

But you need several types. A council of LLMs.

And a router that sends each query to frontier models vs open source ones.

2. GET ONE END-TO-END WORKFLOW RUNNING WITHOUT HUMANS.

That is the tipping point that lets you scale from a handful of agents to hundreds. 

but only if quality is solid first end to end.

Otherwise scaling up is a nightmare.

3. BUILD AN AGENT FACTORY.

Have your agents train and code new agents.

That’s how you go from a couple hundred agents to a thousand.

***TAKEAWAYS FOR MANAGERS:

→ Pick one back office workflow this week, and map it for a full handover to agents.

→ Ask each SaaS vendor how easily you can move your data into a central repository you own.

fullText:
Nice paper on optimizing agents and their graders together.

The key finding is that you want to update your LLM grader alongside the agent instead of keeping it fixed, because the agent's failure modes change as it improves.

DUET alternates between the two.

Each round picks training tasks, runs the solver, has the grader score and critique the trajectories, then a tool-using updater revises either the grader or the solver while the other stays fixed.

On the Finance Agent Benchmark, the solver reaches 96.5%, above GEPA (94.4%) and SkillOpt (94.0%). It also beats both when they optimize against the benchmark's own reference evaluator.

Grader agreement rises from 68.4% to 78.5% on GDPval. Training the grader with the solver frozen moves agreement only from 67.9% to 68.8%.

Paper: https://t.co/qmZBl4RHu5

fullText:
DATA NETWORK EFFECTS DON'T EXIST 98% OF THE TIME

I’ve heard about data moats for years, and I just don’t buy it.

(More on this in my free weekly email, link below.)

Why?

Data leaks, moves around and just gets copied way too easily. 

1. DATA NETWORK EFFECTS ARE MOSTLY JUST THEORY.

The famous flywheel is:

more customers -> more data -> better products 

But this is just standard personalization

That impt but not a network effect.

The only cases that come close for me are search and Waymo.

Which is why I say this idea fails about 98% of the time.

2. DATA SCALE IS REAL BUT A WEAK ADVANTAGE.

The value of more data usually flatlines. 

Each added piece of data is usually worth less.

Increasingly Long tail data tends to decrease in value. 

And Chasing additional data volume often forces you to loosen quality controls

so you get more noise and garbage.

3. PROPRIETARY DATA IS THE EXCEPTION.

It can be a scarce resource competitive advantage.

especially when the data is sold directly as a product.

For example Gartner and the big consulting firms turn past client work into best practices and performance indexes.

I’m a believer.

***TAKEAWAYS FOR MANAGERS:

→ Write down the minimum data your key activities really need

then check what the next batch of data costs you and how fast it goes stale.
